text_blocks.snippet: Losartan can cause mild side effects like dizziness and fatigue, as well as rare, serious risks like high potassium levels.
These symptoms are usually mild and often improve as your body gets used to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly)
Upper respiratory infections or cold symptoms like a stuffy nose or sore throat

text_blocks.snippet: Get medical help right away if you experience any of these rare but dangerous reactions:

list.snippet: Severe allergic reaction (angioedema): Sudden swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing.
High potassium levels (hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, slow pulse, or an irregular heartbeat (though it often causes no symptoms).
Kidney problems: Decreased urination, or swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet.
Very low blood pressure: Extreme lightheadedness or feeling like you might pass out.
Pregnancy: Do not take losartan if you are pregnant because it can cause serious injury or death to an unborn baby.

Dehydration: Severe vomiting, diarrhea, or heavy sweating can lead to dangerous dehydration and kidney issues while on this medication. You can check official details via the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide.
